title: NGC 4490, Barred Spiral Galaxy
caption: The interacting galaxies NGC 4490 and NGC 4485, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter telescope at Kitt Peak
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: The barred spiral galaxy NGC 4490 sits at the center of this image, with a smaller galaxy, NGC 4485, at the upper right. Bright red clouds of gas glow inside both galaxies and in the space between them.
The two are in the early stages of merging. Their mutual gravitational pull is triggering star formation in both galaxies, and those red clouds are where it is happening.

In a barred spiral, a straight band of stars crosses the center and the spiral arms begin near its ends. When two galaxies interact, gravity squeezes their clouds of gas, and dense gas is where new stars form, which is why encounters so often set off bursts of star birth. Over time, pairs like this one are expected to combine into a single larger galaxy, one of the main ways galaxies grow. The pair lies in the constellation Canes Venatici.

understand.summary: The Mosaic camera on the Mayall 4-meter telescope observed the pair through B, V, I and hydrogen-alpha filters, shown as blue, cyan, orange and red respectively.
